content: {"diagnosis": ["I can't render a Christmas tree image in RoboCraft Control Lab - this view is numbers-only.", "Dominant closed-loop pole at -3.45 is slow, gives 0.366s rise and 0.841s settling, just over 0.8s limit.", "Pole at -96.5 is fast/non-dominant, response is well damped with no oscillation.", "65.1 deg phase margin and 5.42 dB gain margin explain 0.0% overshoot.", "Saturation 0.5% at 5V limit is just initial kick, not limiting settling."], "explanation": "You asked for a real-life tree view - I can't add graphics here, only the linear brightness model. Your current PI is stable and smooth because the dominant pole at -3.45 with 65.1 deg phase margin is well damped, so 0.0% overshoot, but that slow -3.45 pole makes settling 0.841s > 0.8s spec. 0.5% saturation is negligible and steady-state error is ~0 due to integral action.", "headline": "No tree view available, and control is stable with 0% overshoot but 0.841s settling just misses 0.8s spec.", "meetsSpecs": false, "proposals": [{"controller": {"N": 20, "Q": [], "R": 1, "kd": 0, "ki": 0.9, "kp": 0.15, "type": "pid"}, "label": "Faster PI", "rationale": "Raise kp to 0.15 and ki to 0.9 to shift -3.45 pole left for <0.8s settling while keeping overshoot <10%."}, {"controller": {"N": 20, "Q": [], "R": 1, "kd": 0.004, "ki": 0.8, "kp": 0.14, "type": "pid"}, "label": "PI-D with small D", "rationale": "Add small kd 0.004 to preserve 60deg+ phase margin with higher P/I for faster settling despite 15ms dead time."}]}
